title: Generating a mouse model for relapsed Sonic Hedgehog medulloblastoma
protocol: Cross Math1-Cre mice with Ptch1loxp/loxp mice to obtain Math1-Cre/Ptch1loxp/wt mice.
Cross Ptch1loxp/loxp mice with R26R-GFP mice to obtain Ptch1loxp/wt/R26R-GFP mice.
Cross Math1-Cre/Ptch1loxp/wt mice with Ptch1loxp/wt/R26R-GFP mice to obtain MPG mice.
Prepare 1 mL of Ketamine (100 mg/mL) at a final concentration of 10 mg/mL under sterile conditions.
Prepare 0.25 mL of Xylazine (20 mg/mL) at a final concentration of 0.5 mg/mL under sterile conditions.
Mix the above solutions with 8.75 mL of saline solution to prepare a final 10 mL anesthetic solution.
Measure body weight of mice using an animal weighing scale.
Inject mice with Ketamine/Xylazine solution (10 μL/g body weight).
Verify lack of pain response by pinching tails (no longer than 10 min after injection) to confirm appropriate depth of anesthesia.
Position the mouse lying prone in a leucite drawer.
Ensure the cerebellum is centered inside of the circular irradiation area.
Expose the cerebellum, but shield the rest of the brain with the lead cover.
Obtain instruction and approval from the Institutional Radiation Safety Committee before using the irradiator machine.
Prepare the irradiator machine as necessary to begin procedures for irradiation of mice.
Ensure there is an air pump to ventilate the drawer for live animals.
Remove lid and place the mouse into the Leucite drawer.
Center the base of the skull inside of the circular irradiation area.
Shield the mouse brain using the lead cover, exposing the cerebellum region.
Cover the drawer with leucite lid.
Set the irradiation time(s) and begin procedure.
Remove mouse from the drawer.
Wipe the leucite drawer with a biocide solution between each mouse irradiation.
Secure irradiator after use.
Place mice on top of warm isothermal pad until they regain upright posture and walk normally.
Return all irradiated mice to a sterilized cage with adequate food and water.
Monitor mice twice daily or more often if poor health is observed.
Anesthetize the mouse by Ketamine/Xylazine as described in step 2a.
Visualize the tumor-bearing brain by MRI using a GE MRI scanner (repetition, 3,450 ms; echo time, 159 ms; 12 slices at 0.8 mm per slice).
Analyze the obtained MRI images using a T2-fast spin echo sequence.
Euthanize mice according to IACUC guidelines.
Decapitate the mouse head with a cut posterior from the ears using surgical scissors.
Make a midline incision in the skin with microdissection scissors.
Peel away the skull to expose the forebrain and cerebellum.
Cut and remove the brain stem (anterior to the cerebellum) and forebrain.
Rinse the cerebellum (containing MB tumor) with PBS.
Place the cerebellum in a 15 mL tube filled with 4% PFA for fixation.
Incubate the cerebellum overnight (∼12 h) at 4°C in 4% PFA.
Transfer the cerebellum from 4% PFA to a new 15 mL tube filled with 30% sucrose.
Dehydrate the cerebellum by incubating it in 30% sucrose for 24 hours or until it sinks to the bottom of the tube.
Embed the cerebellum in optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound.
Freeze the OCT-embedded block at -80°C overnight (∼12 h).
Place the frozen block in a -20°C cryostat for equilibration for at least 1 hour.
Cut 8–12 μm thick frozen sections of the tumor-bearing cerebellum using a cryostat.
Mount the tissue sections on microscope slides.
Rinse the tumor slides with PBST.
Pipette 100 μL of 10% Normal Goat Serum (NGS) to cover the entire section for blocking.
Incubate the slides at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 20–30 minutes for blocking.
Dilute primary antibodies with 10% NGS and pipette 50–100 μL of diluted antibody over the tissue sections.
Incubate the slides overnight (∼12 h) at 4°C in the dark with primary antibodies.
Remove the primary antibody and wash the slides 3× with PBST.
Prepare secondary antibody(s); dilute 1:500 in 10% NGS.
Incubate the slides with secondary antibody for 2 h at room temperature (20°C–25°C), in the dark.
Remove the secondary antibody and wash the slides 3× with PBS.
Counterstain tumor tissue with DAPI to label cell nuclei.
Mount coverslip on tumor slides using mounting medium.
Image slides on a fluorescent microscope to analyze staining results.
